root_idea.summary: The root centers on bringing something out, especially water emerging from or being drawn from the ground.
root_idea.development: The concrete image of water welling forth and being extracted extends to drawing out concealed things, including knowledge. The designation of the Nabataeans is also associated with their extraction of water.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic Form X imperfect is normalized to the standard perfect citation form اِسْتَنْبَطَ.

senses.definition: To extract or elicit knowledge or information from a source; to derive it from those who possess it.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, the extracted matter is obtained from a source or people possessing it, expressed with مِنْهُمْ in 4:83.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To well forth or issue forth, especially of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive verb used of water emerging or flowing out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reach a well’s water and bring it out by digging or other labor; to produce or fetch out the water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a digger reaching the water and transitively of a well or its water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The production of an effect or the making of an impression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative verbal noun meaning the exertion of influence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To imitate the Nabataeans or to claim kinship with them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived Form V use concerning resemblance to or asserted affiliation with the Nabataeans.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw out, extract, produce, fetch out, or extort something by labor, skill, or art.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be physical or something obtained through exertion or ingenuity; the Quranic knowledge use is separately listed above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring a concealed matter to light or make it apparent after it has been hidden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of drawing something out, including eliciting an obscure matter through effort or study.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek to obtain offspring from a mare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative or idiomatic use; one transmitted interpretation connects it with seeking what is in the mare’s belly.
Used of a person becoming identified with the Nabataean people or culture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first water that appears when a well is dug.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the water emerging at the beginning of the digging of a well.
A noun for water obtained through the process of extraction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idioms, a person’s underlying depth or eventual fulfillment; hence a promise whose fulfillment is remote, an unfathomable depth or extent of knowledge, or an inaccessible opponent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are fixed figurative expressions built on the notion of a hidden or difficult-to-reach depth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well whose water has been produced or fetched out by the labor of digging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing the well by reference to the water obtained from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What oozes or exudes from a mountain, like sweat issuing from the sides of rock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of moisture emerging from a mountain or rocky surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Nabataeans; later, by extension, mixed, low, vulgar, or socially inferior people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The original use is an ethnonym; later extended or pejorative applications are also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A white patch beneath a horse’s armpit; an أَنْبَطُ horse is one marked by it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical color marking used in describing a horse.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Reaching and bringing out well water by labor.
Transitive production or extraction of a well’s water.
Imitating or claiming kinship with the Nabataeans.
Form X is linked to drawing out and to the first water emerging from a newly dug well.
Physical extraction, bringing concealed matters to light, and eliciting knowledge are all represented.
The first water appearing in a dug well.
Figurative idioms concerning hidden depth, fulfillment, or inaccessibility.
A well whose water has been obtained by digging.
Moisture oozing from a mountain or rock.
The Nabataeans and later extended social uses.
